solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Run around quickly in small sort of van

parts.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
a camper is a van fitted out for living in

explanation.surface: Someone dashing about in a cramped little camper van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run around quickly in' reads as one phrase, but 'in' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run about quickly and lightly, like a child or a small animal.

clue.text: Boxer possibly trained to do this sort of bicycle

definitions.text: Boxer possibly trained to do this
definitions.meaning: a boxer is a breed of dog; this is a begging trick, rearing back on the haunches with front paws raised
an old-fashioned upright bicycle whose rider sits bolt upright, like a begging dog

explanation.surface: A boxer in training on an exercise bike.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is a dog, not a fighter. A sit-up-and-beg bicycle is the traditional British upright bike with high handlebars.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the dog trick and the upright bicycle are called sit up and beg.

clue.text: Not many misused "bad" for "good", for example

indicators.note: the letters are used wrongly, put into the wrong order

explanation.surface: A grumble that few people misuse slang like 'bad' meaning 'good'.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests slang where 'bad' means 'good'; the definition just wants a word of opposite meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Bad' is the opposite of 'good', so it is an example of an antonym.

clue.text: Quietly show excitement about old luxury flat

parts.note: to enthuse is to show excitement

explanation.surface: Someone trying not to gush too loudly over a grand old apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: P for quietly comes from musical notation (piano). 'Quietly show excitement' reads as one restrained reaction, but 'Quietly' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A penthouse is a luxurious flat on the top floor of a building.

clue.text: Live on edge

explanation.surface: Living with your nerves permanently frayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' looks like one phrase meaning nervous; split it into two words for the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to live somewhere and to have your home there mean the same.

clue.text: An exam to treat with contempt?

definitions.meaning: a practice exam sat before the real one

explanation.surface: A student scornfully dismissing an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a mock is a practice exam sat before the real one.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock is both a trial exam and a verb meaning to ridicule.

clue.text: Samoans corralling flightless bird

indicators.note: the word pens the answer inside itself

parts.note: the letters sit in the middle of the word, after SA and before NS

explanation.surface: Pacific islanders rounding up a large bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The moa was a giant flightless bird of New Zealand, now extinct.
explanation.definitionFit: The moa was a huge bird that could not fly.

clue.text: In deep sleep, minute butterfly

indicators.note: 'In' says the next piece sits inside the sleep word

parts.note: a coma is a deep unconsciousness

explanation.surface: A tiny butterfly fast asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like 'tiny' describing the butterfly; it is the abbreviation for a unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The comma is a British butterfly named for a white comma-shaped mark on its wing.

clue.text: Giant bird with a name

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A huge bird that has been given a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giant bird' looks like one phrase for an ostrich or moa; 'Giant' alone is the definition, and the bird is a tiny one.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a giant, after the Titans of Greek myth.

clue.text: What insects may have done as south got hotter

parts.note: to warm is to get hotter

explanation.surface: Bugs gathering as the southern weather heated up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' only joins the definition to the wordplay; the definition is a description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees and other insects swarm when they gather in a dense moving mass.

clue.text: Never fear a battleship

parts.note: nought = nothing, not at all, as in 'never'

explanation.surface: A slogan of courage, then a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship's name literally means 'fear nothing', which 'Never fear' paraphrases; the two halves are read in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Dreadnought gave her name to a whole class of big-gun battleships.

clue.text: Run smartly back for tack

indicators.note: 'back' says go back the way you came, reading the letters right to left

parts.note: to nip is to go somewhere quickly, as in 'nip to the shops'

explanation.surface: A sailor told to hurry back and change tack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tack' looks nautical; it is the small nail, which a pin can stand for.
explanation.definitionFit: A tack is a short pin or nail used to fasten things.

clue.text: Commissioned exactly what's required and was sure of success

definitions.meaning: got something made to order, read literally word by word
idiom: to have it made is to be certain of success

explanation.surface: A client orders a bespoke item and feels their success is guaranteed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is the literal reading of the phrase, the second its idiomatic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who had it made was set up to succeed without difficulty.

clue.text: Ordinary people, those fools

explanation.surface: A snob dismissing ordinary people as idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: The break falls differently in wordplay and answer: THEM + ASSES regroups as THE MASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed phrase for the general public, as opposed to an elite.

clue.text: Students receiving substantial amount of storage in the cloud

indicators.note: whatever is receiving something takes it in, so the students hold the storage inside them

parts.note: 1MB, one megabyte, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Students getting plenty of cloud storage for their files.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storage in the cloud' reads as online computing; the cloud is the definition. NUS is the UK's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteorological term for a dark grey rain-bearing cloud.

clue.text: Came across bricklayer's tool and how to use it?

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them
a hod is an open box on a pole for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: Finding a hod and wondering how to use it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' in the definition points back to the hod, so the clue hangs together as one scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A way or procedure for doing something, so it tells you how to use the tool.

clue.text: Emergency resource in hotel is out of order

indicators.note: the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: The hotel's emergency phone is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container instruction; it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotline is a direct phone line for emergencies or urgent help.

clue.text: Prejudiced bishop cast aside

indicators.note: the letters are thrown, cast about, into a new order

parts.note: B = bishop, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: A prejudiced bishop being thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast aside' looks like one phrase meaning rejected; 'cast' is the anagram signal working on 'aside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean leaning unfairly for or against someone.

clue.text: Book all-Ireland ace dancer

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Booking a star dancer for an all-Ireland competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb, to hire; it is only B.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: she is a female ballet dancer.

clue.text: Contract to rent meadows with house at the rear

indicators.note: take the letter at the back of 'house'

explanation.surface: Renting some fields with a house behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House at the rear' reads as a building behind the fields; only the last letter of 'house' is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is a contract letting someone rent property.

clue.text: Number required to constitute company?

parts.note: reads like a legal minimum of members for forming something
the surface pushes a business firm; the setter means company as in having someone with you, as in the proverb about a crowd

explanation.surface: A question about the minimum number of people needed to form a business.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd' supplies the number; the question mark flags the shift from business to friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says two's company, so two people is the number needed.

clue.text: Girls following grand spectacles

explanation.surface: Girls trailing behind a grand show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectacles' looks like grand shows; here they are eyeglasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles and glasses are both lenses worn to correct vision.

clue.text: Cat shortly coming up to drink

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter
in a down entry, the letters read upwards

parts.note: PUSS, a cat, loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A cat soon to come up and lap at a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: PUSS is a familiar word for a cat; in a down clue 'coming up' turns the shortened word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To sup is to drink, taking small mouthfuls.

clue.text: Undercover police operation hurt a little

definitions.meaning: a trap in which police pose as criminals
cause a sharp but brief pain

explanation.surface: A police raid in which someone got slightly injured.
explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated meanings sit side by side; the police sense comes from con-artist slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Sting names both a police trap and a brief sharp pain.

clue.text: Carry on, but glance back

indicators.note: 'back' says go back the way you came, reading the letters right to left

parts.note: a peek is a quick glance

explanation.surface: Advice to keep walking but look over your shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glance back' reads as looking behind you; it signals PEEK read the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of continue, as in keeping going.

clue.text: Remove perfume? That's a comedown

parts.note: the prefix de- means to remove, as in de-ice

explanation.surface: Someone stripped of their perfume, finding it a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: DE-SCENT would mean to remove the scent, which the question mark flags as a playful coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fall in status is both a going down and a comedown.
